## Phase 1: Intuition Playground

Adjust the slider below to project the 2D neural firing rates onto different vectors. Observe how the projected variance changes as the projection angle rotates:

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 450

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput("angle", "Projection Angle (degrees):", min = 0, max = 180, value = 45),
  plotOutput("projPlot")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  set.seed(42)
  x <- rnorm(60)
  y <- 0.8 * x + rnorm(60, sd = 0.5)
  data_mat <- cbind(x, y)
  
  output$projPlot <- renderPlot({
    theta <- input$angle * pi / 180
    v <- c(cos(theta), sin(theta))
    proj <- data_mat %*% v
    
    par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
    plot(x, y, pch = 19, col = "steelblue", asp = 1,
         main = "Scatter Plot & Projection Vector", xlab = "Neuron 1", ylab = "Neuron 2")
    arrows(0, 0, 2 * v[1], 2 * v[2], col = "red", lwd = 2)
    
    hist(proj, breaks = 12, col = "salmon", 
         main = paste("Projected Variance:", round(var(proj), 2)),
         xlab = "Projected Coordinates", xlim = c(-3, 3))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## Phase 2: Fix-It Lab

### Challenge 1: The Dominant Channel Bug
In multi-channel recordings, channels with massive baseline voltages can dominate the principal components if data are not normalized.

Run the code below and inspect the variance explained by PC1:

```r
# Simulate 5 channels where channel 1 has 100x the raw amplitude
raw_channels <- cbind(
  ch1 = rnorm(50, mean = 500, sd = 50),
  ch2 = rnorm(50, mean = 5, sd = 1),
  ch3 = rnorm(50, mean = 5, sd = 1),
  ch4 = rnorm(50, mean = 5, sd = 1),
  ch5 = rnorm(50, mean = 5, sd = 1)
)

# BUG: scale. is currently set to FALSE
pca_bad <- prcomp(raw_channels, scale. = FALSE)
summary(pca_bad)

# TASK: Change scale. to TRUE and compare the proportion of variance explained!
```
